ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in right triangle $ABC$, the right-angle sides $AC=3\text{cm}$ and $BC=4\text{cm}$. Let $P$ and $Q$ be points moving along $AB$ and $BC$, respectively. Point $P$ moves from point $A$ towards point $B$ at a constant speed, while point $Q$ moves from point $B$ towards point $C$ at the same constant speed of $1\text{cm}$ per second. The movement of $P$ stops as soon as $Q$ reaches point $C$. Let the movement time of $P$ and $Q$ be $t$ seconds. For what value of $t$ is $\triangle PBQ$ an isosceles triangle with $\angle B$ as the vertex angle?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the leg $AC=3\text{cm}$ and $BC=4\text{cm}$,\\
thus, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have $AB=\sqrt{AC^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5$,\\
therefore, $AP=t$ and $BP=5-t$, $BQ=t$,\\
since $\triangle PBQ$ is an isosceles triangle with $\angle B$ as the vertex angle,\\
thus, $BP=BQ$, that is, $5-t=t$, solving this gives $t=\boxed{\frac{5}{2}}$ seconds,\\
therefore, when $t=\boxed{\frac{5}{2}}$ seconds, $\triangle PBQ$ forms an isosceles triangle with $\angle B$ as the vertex angle.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows right triangle ABC with B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and A above C. Segment BC is horizontal, segment AC is vertical, so the right angle is at C. Segment AB is the slanted hypotenuse. Point P lies on AB between A and B, and point Q lies on BC between B and C; segment PQ is drawn inside the triangle. Reasoning: From the given lengths, AC = 3 cm and BC = 4 cm are the right-angle sides, so AB = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5 cm. Both points move at 1 cm/s. The stopping condition is t <= 4 because Q reaches C after 4 seconds, and 5/2 <= 4, so this value is valid.
